description.narrative: Sida's Core-support to KCSF, Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, will contribute to the organization's goal of a meaningful and sustainable engagement of civil society in socio-economic development processes that serve the public good. The vision with KCSF-s work is to see Kosovo as a prosperous, inclusive and democratic society with an advanced process of EU integration. The support will enable KCSF to work both with policies and research for input to for example the government, and with other non-governmental organizations in supporting them with their own operations in order to contribute and push for a democratic development. The support from Sweden also enables KCSF to forwarding funds through the Pool Funding Mechanism EJA (Engagement for joint action) to small and medium sized organization in the country.

Sidas kärnstöd 2024-2028, till KCSF, Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, ska bidra till organisationens mål om ett meningsfullt och hållbart engagemang från civilsamhället i socioekonomiska utvecklingsprocesser som tjänar medborgarnas bästa. Visionen med KCSF:s arbete är att se Kosovo som ett välmående, inkluderande och demokratiskt samhälle med en avancerad process för EU-integration. Stödet ska göra det möjligt för KCSF att arbeta både med policys och forskning för input till exempelvis regeringen, och med andra icke-statliga organisationer för att stödja dem med sin egen verksamhet för att bidra och driva på en demokratisk utveckling. Stödet från Sverige gör det också möjligt för KCSF att vidarebefordra medel genom Pool Funding Mechanism EJA (Engagemang för gemensamma åtgärder) till små och medelstora organisationer i landet.

The partner, KCSF, has presented a five level Theory of change, with the Vision on the top, followed by Strategic goal/mission, Medium Term objectives, intermediate objectives and then the KCSF functions.
The vision of the work KCSF is "Kosovo is a prosperous, inclusive, and democratic society with an advanced process of EU integration". The vision is then linked to the strategic goal for KCSF to engage the civil society in a meaningful and sustainable way, in socio-economic development processes that serve the public good.
To reach the strategic goal KCSF will, as part of the medium term objectives, build capacity of civil society organizations - such as enhancing their knowledge, support them with diverse resources (also grants), connecting them to different actors and offering platforms and coordination. KCSF's work to improve the legal framework on a government level is also part of this medium term objective with the strive for civil society to be part of public processes and strengthening new laws and so forth.
The medium term objectives can only be reached if also new actors (new partners for KCSF) are engaged. Therefore, for the new core-phase, KCSF has added intermediate objectives to their theory of change, meaning outreach and cooperation with private sector and diaspora to make them more engaged in the civil society development in Kosovo. On this level KCSF will also reach out to more civil servants and politicians in order to enhance their knowledge about legal aspects and willingness to engage meaningful with civil society.
All these levels will be reached through KCSF's hands-on work and functions; such as mobilizing and providing adequate financial resources, strengthening capacity to enable a participatory civil society engagement and continuing cooperating with already engaged partners, and new different actors, in the improvement and development of the system for civil society to act.
During the new phase of core-support - until 2028 - KCSF foresee a strengthened civil society, incorporating new actors within the private sector and with the diaspora.

title.narrative: Grant agrement between Sida and Kosovar Civil Society Foundation
Decision on Contribution - Core support to Kosovar Civil Society Foundation 2024-2028

description.narrative:
KCSF has achieved good results during 2025 despite some unexpected challenges, that is worth mentioning, as the results also needs to be viewed with those challenges in mind. Firstly, in January, USAID unexpectedly closed their operations and support, with immediate loss of funding for their partners (in total according to KCSF's research 28,22 MUSD). In Kosovo, the civil society in general was negatively affected by this, with 68 agreements being terminated, impacting 40 organisations. Also KCSF was affected by this, with a 44 % reduction of the planned annual budget for 2025 and as a consequence of that KCSF had to let go of 12 staff. The other main challenge was the inconclusive results from the national elections in February 2025, which halted a lot of planned reforms and also affected the civil society's ability to participate in consultations and to do advocacy towards national level policies and processes.
In order to mitigate some of the negative effects of the funding cuts, Sida could add additional funding to the EJA mechanism through an amendment of agreement, adding 360 000 EURO to the budget. This enabled KCSF to increase the number of grantees for their 3-year institutional grant.
Results based on the three intermediate objectives:
1. Civil society has adequate and diverse resources and capacity to engage
2. Civil society has a legitimate support base and relations to successfully engage
3. The legal framework that encourages civil society to operate freely and engage in public processes is respected and practiced.
Due to USAIDs withdrawal, the funding landscape drastically affected civil society actors across Kosovo. Therefore KCSF prioritised maintaining and expanding the EJA regranting mechanism and disbursed approximately 1,3 MEURO across 65 grants, and initiated a second insittutional grants call during Q4 2025 (agreements with the new grantees signed in Q1 2026), with the help of Sida's approval of a budget increase. The Hans Wilsdorf foundation also confirmed its entry into EJA during 2025, contributing funds for civil society for 2026-2028. KCSF also managed to launch a Civic Emergeny Fund for the Western Balkans and Croatia together with Trag Foundation, extending their work on rapid response support in the region.
The political deadliock also affected the ability of civil society actors to engage with and advocate decision makers at different levels. Furthermore, the Online platform for public consultations was dysfunctional parts of the year, which also negatively impacted civil society to give input to policy development and participate through consultations.
Despite this situation, KCSF's assessment is that the capacity of civil society organisations to a large extent have been strengthened (and in some cases sustained), with demonstrated improvements in staff skills and transparency, for example. An increased number of citizens were active or a member in a civil society organisation compared to 2024. KCSF's capacity building initiative School of Activitism engaged nearly 60 representatives from 22 CSOs.
Through its coordination of advocacy and policy efforts, KCSF also monitors civic space in Kosovo, delivering seven reports where they covered around 200 key developments concerning civic space. This has also been fed into CIVICUS Monitor.
The advocacy efforts have also led to specific results, despite the political deadlock. To name a few, one highlight was the government approved Emergency telephone line for victims of domestic violence, violence against women and gender-based violence, after advocacy and consultations, where a licensed NGO runts a free, 24-hour service. Anotehr one was the inclusion of Kosovo in hte European Economic and Social Committee's enlargement Candidate Members initiative, after consorted efforts by more than a hundred CSO:s from the region, and coordinated through BCSDN. The consorted efforts by many CSO:s, coordinated by KCSF, impacted the drafting of the government strategy for cooperation with Civil Society 2026-2031, the draft will then be open for public consultations during 2026.
The EJA grant mechanism functioned as planned and offered continuity and predictability for civil society support throughout 2025 and was even expanded due to extra funding from Sida to top up the existing funding and allow for more grants. Through the way it is managed, the EJA mechanism is a trusted mechanism for long-term, flexible funding. During 2025 EJA disbursed 1 304 842 Eur across 65 grants through the different grant opportunities that are part of EJA. Recipients were more established civil society organisations as well as grassroot initiatives and activists across the country. During 2025, EJA exceeded it geographical balance commitments, and reaching communities across Kosovo, with a strong focus on actors based outside Prishtina and including minority communities.
